title: Quad-layout carve (layout embedding) stage: 0.67 s to under 100 ms
description:
Make the `carve` stage of QuadLayoutEngine fast. It takes 0.674 s today. Log: embed arcs=6792 on a V=38480 F=76976 copy, carve 0.55 s and check 0.03 s; chord snapping laid 7405 chords. Baseline, measured 2026-10-15 with `uv run ixdar-cli run-scene --scene quad-layout --property quadLayoutScene.alpha=15` on the default model (headless, 9.1 s to ready): cross field 0.395 s, seamless 0.800 s, motorcycle graph 0.145 s, quantization 1.526 s, carve 0.674 s, contract 1.475 s, global grid map 1.897 s. These run synchronously before the scene's first frame, so together they are almost all of the quad-layout scene's time to first paint. The user's goal is first paint under 0.1 s; a sibling ticket moves the pipeline off the first frame, and each stage ticket makes one stage as fast as it can go. Target: this stage under 100 ms on the default model, or as close as the algorithm allows, with the reason it can go no lower. The stage's output must not change: same singularity count, arc/node/patch counts, quad count and a screenshot that image-diffs clean against the master baseline. Use the stage's own `[quad-layout] <stage>` log line and an async-profiler capture (`run-scene --profile`, read with `ixdar-cli profile-report`). Stay inside this stage's package; touch shared code (solver/, HalfEdgeMesh, QuadLayoutEngine) only where the stage needs it, and list every shared-file change in the report, because six sibling tickets run in parallel. Related: CRAW-2 (scan-scale pipeline), CRAW-4 (cached layouts).

Round 2 (user request 2026-10-15). Round 1 (storage and lookup rework) is committed in the worktree as c4539ee0; botijo carve 0.62 -> 0.47 s cold, but hand/feline/buddha screenshots differ from master (22/34/295 px, counts identical), so round 1 is not yet output-identical. Algorithmic waste spanning carve and contract: on botijo carve embeds 6792 arcs, 4493 of them quantised to zero length; contraction (LCBK19 Section 6.1) collapses them, splitting edges to drag survivors, and recarve then re-embeds only 908 arcs / 454 patches. ~85% of the carve is built only to be torn down; carve + contract are ~1.4 s on botijo. Idea: contract the T-mesh combinatorially (zero-arc collapse, zero-patch split/collapse as graph operations on the quantised T-mesh, in parameter space) BEFORE any surface embedding, then carve the contracted ~900-arc layout once. PATCH-120 notes the contracted layout is a fixed point the paper proves order-independent combinatorially. PATCH-119 (archived) tried merging zero-node clusters before the embedding but still carved and routed along traces and measured contraction splits (-27%..+11%); it never skipped the carve. The user recalls several earlier attempts at this route with little success; no ticket or commit for them was found.

Singularity count, arc/node/patch counts and quad count match master exactly. 3. A screenshot of the final layout under tmp/ image-diffs clean against a master screenshot taken the same way. 4. No debugging scaffolding is left behind; `ixd wt done` passes.

5. Every mesh reports MATCH against the master baseline: the same status (a mesh master fails on must fail the same way), the same count signature, and an identical screenshot. The per-mesh stage times before/after go in changes-made. A DIFF stops for a user ruling.

Round 2: round 1 is output-identical to master on the whole suite; the combinatorial-contraction prototype is reported with its counts per suite mesh against master's recarve, whatever the outcome; if wired in, it sits behind a switch defaulting to the current path until the user rules, with carve+contract time and per-mesh count/energy comparison recorded.

Not landed; waiting on investigation/ruling.

Round 2 step 0, round 1 made output-identical. Cause: SnappingCarve.collectCrossings numbered the crossed constraint edges with HashMap.get/put, while master filled its Map<Long, List<int[]>> with computeIfAbsent. HashMap.computeIfAbsent links a new key at the HEAD of its hash bucket, put links it at the TAIL, so on keys that collide in a bucket the two maps iterate in opposite orders. The edge order fixes the order grantCorners and mintLanes run in, hence which arc wins a contested corner and the ids of minted lane vertices: same counts, slightly different chords (hand 22 px, feline 34, buddha 295). Ruled out first by in-place checks on hand (all zero mismatches): faceCorner vs HalfEdgeMesh.faceVertexAt, the present-chord shortcut in extendPathByChord (disabled: still DIFF), the recorded-edge lookup in ArcNetwork.assemble, exitBarycentric through copy corners. Fix (uncommitted, SnappingCarve only): number the edges with computeIfAbsent, comment says why. Suite (tmp/quad-suite/craw-70-r2 vs master-0f52d26f): 14/14 MATCH, screenshots identical. Stage times master -> worktree, carve: sphere_base 0.058->0.024, bolt 0.134->0.072, hand 0.26->0.188, elk 0.522->0.315, feline 1.289->0.479, fertility 0.452->0.251, botijo 0.665->0.408, block 0.423->0.295, Hand-tri-30k 0.355->0.282, rockerarm 0.45->0.248, buddha 1.076->0.762; contract (not touched by this diff, single unlocked-order runs, noisy): botijo 1.346->0.782, buddha 2.985->1.39.

Round 2 step 1, prior art (archive/* tags were listable with git for-each-ref). (a) quantization/ZeroArcCollapse (2026-06-12, 'mesh Layout first pass') and LayoutExtraction (still on master): a union-find of the end nodes of every zero arc after quantization (Lyon 2021 Section 6 'collapse half'); it gives the final NODE set (block: clusters=154 = recarve nodes 154) but not the final arcs (block 1129 skeleton arcs vs 316 after contraction) because it never applies the zero-patch operators, and it never fed an embedding. (b) ZeroElementContraction (2026-07-13, deleted 07-24): took LayoutExtraction's clusters and contracted each onto an anchor (the critical member, else lowest id) ON THE EMBEDDED MESH by node moves and re-routes; replaced by the local LCBK19 operators (ZeroArcCollapseOperator etc., 07-16). (c) Worktrees zero-web-collapse (Aug 16, uncommitted FanPolygonCollapse: dissolve a moving node's whole fan and redraw its arcs as chords) and contract-churn (Aug 15, no diff): embedded-collapse variants, not combinatorial. (d) PATCH-119 (archive/patch-119, d9ca1f04): merged all-zero non-critical nodes before the carve and routed survivors along concatenated traces; zero clusters are sub-triangle tight, so concatenated routes U-turn across one constraint edge or lose shared crossings next to a node, chords cross, merges get frozen and re-sliced: only 6/16 merges survive on bolt, 52/501 botijo; splits -27%..+11%; recarve counts equal master. It never skipped the carve and never ran operators 2/3 combinatorially. (e) Coordinator session d8f46ba8 (2026-09-19..26) argued that operators 2/3 make zero-AREA patches (one side zero) into curves and must survive, pointed at MPZ14 whole-chain collapse and at LCK21a Section 6's alternative (locate each trace's closest non-separated singularity by a path search on the T-mesh and trace the separatrix, RRP15 6.1) which embeds only final arcs. No commit, branch or ticket ever built a full combinatorial operators-1-to-3 contraction; the earlier failures were all at the EMBEDDING of merged nodes (where to route survivors through tight clusters), not at the combinatorics.

Round 2 step 2, prototype (compare only, pipeline untouched): embedding/CombinatorialContraction.java copies the quantized arrangement's combinatorics the way ArcNetwork.assemble revives them (same ids, arcs live when they bound a patch), then runs NetworkContraction's rounds operator for operator with no paths: operator 3 (ready bigon, survivor feature-else-lower-id) first, else operator 1 on the lowest-id collapsible zero arc (Def 6.2 moving endpoint, fewer-arcs-then-lower-id, merge = mergeNodeInto, loop removal = removeCollapsedArc incl. the pinched-patch splice), else operator 2 (T-joint extension through a non-simple zero patch, splitting the opposite arc at the quantized offset); then LCK21a Section 6 T-junction extension. Driver: test/benchmark/CombinatorialContractionBenchmark (-Dbenchmark.off=<mesh>, alpha 15) also steps the embedded contraction recording every moved->surviving node, conforms, recarves, and compares. Its recarve counts equal the suite logs on every mesh. Merged-node placement: a cluster's critical member when it has one (Def 6.2: critical nodes never move; the quantization's separation constraints keep one per cluster), else the member nearest the cluster centroid (the paper fixes no order, A.3 only proves termination; every member has the same quantized position, so the medoid minimises how far surviving arcs travel). Results, comb vs recarve nodes/arcs/patches, then ops, comb time vs carve+contract(+recarve) in the same JVM, clusters, placement distance (rep vs where recarve puts the cluster, in mean input edge lengths): sphere_base 30/56/28 = 30/56/28 MATCH, 312 collapses 106 bigons 0 splits 0 ext, 0.007 vs 0.024+0.038 s, 30/30 clusters identical, rep=survivor 12/30, median 0.42 p95 3.27 max 3.44 | bolt 44/84/42 MATCH, 186/90/3/14, 0.006 vs 0.062+0.069, 36/36 identical, 24/32, 0.00/0.82/1.03 | hand 677/1350/675 MATCH, 1703/857/6/204, 0.059 vs 0.148+0.282, 488/488, 168/382, 0.17/2.23/16.92 | elk 476/952/476 MATCH, 3457/1328/11/92, 0.089 vs 0.314+0.538, 397/397, 143/359, 0.20/2.60/5.12 | feline 1981/3966/1983 MATCH, 6032/2761/26/735, 0.171 vs 0.478+0.836, 1279/1279, 433/1072, 0.13/1.61/13.80 | fertility 248/508/254 MATCH, 2286/801/0/12, 0.070 vs 0.250+0.491, 239/239, 95/231, 0.21/4.19/11.55 | botijo 446/908/454 MATCH, 4512/1572/17/87, 0.094 vs 0.405+0.753, 371/371, 147/349, 0.21/2.83/5.31 | block 160/328/164 MATCH, 2904/810/0/0, 0.092 vs 0.266+0.591, 160/160, 66/159, 0.28/12.72/15.70 | Hand-tri-30k 320/636/318 MATCH, 2356/849/7/114, 0.072 vs 0.267+0.452, 215/215, 81/193, 0.30/3.41/5.53 | rockerarm (fig 8 and fig 9 identical) 201/402/201 MATCH, 891/382/5/50, 0.018 vs 0.236+0.830, 158/158, 62/126, 0.01/4.54/10.52 | buddha 2500/4996/2498 MATCH, 3650/2101/18/962, 0.112 vs 0.734+1.296, 1567/1567, 416/1162, 0.69/9.92/24.87. No positive-length arc ever closed into a loop. Counts AND merge clusters match on every completing mesh (fandisk, sphere_random and crawfish fail before the carve on master too). Placement: the recarve's survivor is order-dependent (shortest-zero-arc-first plus fewer-arcs-moves), so a deterministic representative agrees with it in 35-75% of merged clusters; median offset under one mean edge everywhere, but the tail is long (block p95 12.7, buddha max 24.9 mean edges): long zero chains.

Round 2 step 3, milestone 1 (uncommitted, behind QuadLayoutEngine.carveContractedLayout, default false): embedding/ContractedLayoutCarve merges zero-arc clusters combinatorially BEFORE the carve, carves the merged layout once on a fresh copy (SnappingCarve recarve-style entry), and hands it to the unchanged NetworkContraction (rounds for the leftovers, conform, recarve). Routing without concatenation: a cluster (union-find over zero arcs, at most one critical/border member) is admitted only when it fits one source face (node at its pinned member or the member nearest the centroid) or one vertex star (node on that vertex); each surviving arc keeps its own trace slice up to where it leaves that region and then runs as one straight chord to the node, checked in barycentric coordinates against every surviving trace piece and node in the face, and faces are claimed so regions are disjoint. CombinatorialContraction gained collapsibleByArc (mask) and collapse() (operators 3 and 1 only). SnappingCarve: sliceArc refactored into public slicePassages(strip, trace, from, to, startVertex, endVertex), same passages. Result: valid, counts equal master: bolt 44/84/42, botijo 446/908/454. But admission is low: bolt 16/32 clusters, botijo 52/349 clusters (244 collapsible arcs of ~4500 zero arcs; 12 one-face regions), so no time is saved (botijo carve 0.52 s, contract 0.70 s vs 0.41 + 0.78 default). Most zero arcs sit in geometrically wide clusters: zero-width ladders (two parallel traces with zero separation, every rung a 2-node cluster whose rails then collapse as bigons) and long zero chains. Next idea, not built: admit after a scratch full collapse so the survivors are known, put the node on the member where the surviving arcs already end, and extend an arc's slice along ITS OWN trace through the cluster's collinear zero arcs (a ladder's outer transversal arc runs straight on through the dead rung; no turn, no shared piece); only arcs that would need a turn onto another trace still need a chord or lane offset.

Round 2 step 3, switch-off check: whole suite (tmp/quad-suite/craw-70-r3-off vs master-0f52d26f) 14/14 MATCH with carveContractedLayout off and the SnappingCarve slicePassages refactor in place; the default path stays output-identical to master.

Round 2 gate A (botijo, 'next idea' built as straight admission): scratch full combinatorial contraction learns each cluster's survivors; a cluster is admitted when every surviving incident arc reaches one member (the critical/border member when there is one) along its OWN trace through the cluster's dead zero arcs, the node sits on that member and each arc's slice is extended to it (no chords, no concatenation); validate-and-reject: re-run the masked combinatorial collapse with rejected clusters' zero arcs left standing and re-check every cluster until stable. Ceiling (scratch contraction, arcs from operator-2 splits / T-junction extensions ignored): botijo 246/349 straight (231 with the critical member pinned), 66 more need exactly one turning end, 52 need two or more; buddha 1095/1162 (1078 pinned). Masked first round: botijo 222/349 admitted (64%), buddha 1032/1162 (89%). The reject loop then cascades to ZERO on both (botijo 222->72->8->0 in 4 rounds, buddha 1032->805->594->405->256->160->86->32->6->0): clusters are chained through bigons along zero ladders and chains, so leaving one rejected cluster's zero arcs standing keeps its neighbours' parallel rails alive, and those rails reach the neighbour at a member off its center (a turn). The rejected ones are dominated by the critical clusters: on botijo every singularity tested had a 12-63 member zero cluster with 4 of its 5 surviving arcs straight and one that must turn onto another trace. Time with the switch on (single run, admission 0 after the loop): botijo carve 0.62 s / contract 0.75 s vs default 0.42 / 0.78; buddha 1.24 / 1.29. Gate A fails (admission under 80%, and the turning ends that would keep the rest admitted are the long tight critical clusters where PATCH-119's routes U-turned and crossed), so the path is removed. What blocked it: the contracted layout's survivors are only consistent when EVERY cluster collapses, so a partial (validate-and-reject) admission cannot work; a future attempt must route every turning end (about 224 on botijo, 125 on buddha, mostly the one off-trace arc of each singularity cluster) along the dead zero arcs' traces with lane offsets, i.e. solve the PATCH-119 routing problem for the whole layout at once, or find a contraction order whose survivors are all straight.

Round 2 removal: the combinatorial-contraction path is gone (CombinatorialContraction, ContractedLayoutCarve, CombinatorialContractionBenchmark deleted; QuadLayoutEngine.carveContractedLayout switch removed, QuadLayoutEngine back to its committed state; SnappingCarve sliceArc/nodeBarycentric restored to their pre-prototype private signatures). Kept: round 1 (c4539ee0) and the step-0 SnappingCarve fix (edge numbering via computeIfAbsent, so colliding hash keys iterate in master's order). Whole suite tmp/quad-suite/craw-70-final vs master-0f52d26f: 14/14 MATCH (same status, count signature and screenshot; sphere_random, fandisk, Hand-tri-30k and crawfish fail to load exactly as on master).

Round 3 (user question: why EmbeddedMeshTopology had edgeJoins and faceCorner instead of a fast mesh). Synced onto 599d7773 (MESH-52: HalfEdgeMesh adjacency packed into IntIdTable flat rows), no conflicts. With faceVertices/faceHalfEdges/vertexEdges now flat rows, the embedding no longer needs its own walks over mesh-internal arrays: deleted EmbeddedMeshTopology.faceCorner (all callers in EmbeddedMeshTopology and FaceStripPath use HalfEdgeMesh.faceVertexAt, rows start at faceHalfEdge and follow the loop, so the corners are the same) and EmbeddedMeshTopology.edgeJoins (ArcNetwork.assemble and LayoutEmbedding.assertSubcomplex are back to master's plain edgeBetween/requireEdge; edgeBetween is a scan of the vertex's flat vertexEdges row, so no separate recorded-edge query is needed and HalfEdgeMesh/MeshTopology are unchanged). Removed every remaining direct read of HalfEdgeMesh arrays (faceHalfEdge[], halfEdgeNext/Twin/Edge/Face/Vertex[]) from embedding/: ArcNetwork orientation flood, PatchCorridor.floodWithin and ArcRerouter.tryRoute now iterate faceHalfEdgeCount/faceHalfEdgeAt and use the halfEdgeEdge/Twin/Face/Vertex/EndVertex accessors (the last two were master code with comments justifying the arrays by the old per-face lists). No shared file changed. Timing, botijo alpha=15, master 599d7773 vs worktree interleaved under the suite lock (load 6-9): cold carve master 0.892/0.622/0.606 (median 0.622) vs worktree 0.547/0.614/0.550 (median 0.550); round-2 worktree recorded 0.529/0.557/0.609, so no regression. Warm (one JVM, 5 recomputes, two runs per side): worktree 0.238/0.175/0.180/0.151/0.148 and 0.532/0.335/0.399/0.307/0.363 (second run under heavy load), master 0.296/0.334/0.340/0.253/0.217 and 0.395/0.271/0.241/0.279/0.272. Screenshots identical both sides (sha 532838bbe012). Whole suite: new master baseline tmp/quad-suite/master-599d7773 (MESH-52 changed screenshots vs master-0f52d26f, e.g. botijo 22e54fa9 -> 532838bb, so the old baseline no longer applies), then tmp/quad-suite/craw-70-r3 --compare master-599d7773: 14/14 MATCH (same status, count signature, identical screenshot; sphere_random, fandisk, Hand-tri-30k and crawfish fail to load exactly as on master). mvn test: 487 run, 0 failures. ixd wt done craw-70 passed (it synced onto abc1c72a, IX-25 colour audit, which touches no embedding/ file), ticket REVIEW.
